question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}(x+1), & \,2\le x\le 4, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}, & \,1\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\ge 3,Y\le 4).$
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(x+1)\cdot \frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x+1}{4{y}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [2,4]\times [1,2].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{4{y}^{2}}, & \,2\le x\le 4,\,1\le y\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3,Y\le 4) & ={\int }_{3}^{4}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{x+1}{4{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{x+1}{4}{[-\frac{1}{y}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{x+1}{4}(\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{x+1}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{8}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+x)]}_{3}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(8+4)-\frac{1}{8}(\frac{9}{2}+3) \\  & =\frac{9}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
